clue.text: Each tribunal formed is severe in judging

indicators.note: formed says the letters of the two words are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A tribunal set up for each case proves harsh in its judgements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' is the anagram signal, rearranging all twelve letters of EACH TRIBUNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being harsh and unkind in how you judge others is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Flawed United Nations measure

parts.note: to sound is to measure the depth of water

explanation.surface: A United Nations resolution is criticised as defective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsound is defective or flawed, like an argument with holes.

clue.text: Apples in crates — 100 for bishop

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Apples arrive in crates, a hundred of them for the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox's Orange Pippin is a British apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Cox's Orange Pippins are a well-known variety of eating apple, called Coxes for short.

clue.text: Team leader, Greek character with letters, reportedly

parts.note: alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for letters is heard rather than seen

parts.note: mail is letters delivered by the post

explanation.surface: A team captain, a Greek, deals with correspondence according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: The dominant member of a group is its leader, from animal behaviour studies.

clue.text: Edible seaweed served up in club

parts.note: nori is the edible seaweed used in sushi

explanation.surface: Seaweed is dished up at a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with an angled metal head is named after its material.

clue.text: A suitable one, salesman sent over drink before meal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A suitable salesman sends over a drink before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent over' turns the three pieces together, giving PERITIF; the opening A stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken to stimulate appetite before eating, from the French.

clue.text: One filling in for actor Herbert, entertaining copper

parts.note: Herbert Lom was a Czech-born British actor, of the Pink Panther films
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer here; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily stands in for another.

clue.text: Board not erected offering food for fish

indicators.note: erected says the word is set upright, read upwards in a down answer

explanation.surface: A board not put up becomes fish food.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny drifting organisms in water are eaten by many fish.

clue.text: Female entertainer his age? Possibly

indicators.note: Possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A hostess wonders whether it is his age that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation is a female entertainer.

clue.text: Ten in a shop stirred by single musical instrument

indicators.note: in places the Roman ten inside the mixed letters
stirred says the letters of the two words are mixed up

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Something in a shop is jumbled up alongside a lone musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' rearranges the letters into SAOPH, and 'in' sets the Roman ten within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed woodwind used in jazz is an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: First of leopardesses in hollow to give birth

indicators.note: in places the opening letter within the word for a hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

indicators.note: First of picks only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The leading female leopard retreats into a cave to have her cubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a calf is giving birth, said of cows, whales and elephants.

clue.text: Throw a Parisian group when answer entered

indicators.note: entered says the letter for answer goes into the word for group

explanation.surface: A French gang throws someone when a reply is given.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from a horse is to dislodge them from the saddle.

clue.text: Servant returned don's crumpled suit

indicators.note: returned says the word for servant is read backwards
crumpled says the letters of the word are scrunched into a new order

explanation.surface: A maid came back to find a university fellow's suit all creased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives DIAM; 'crumpled' turns DONS into ONDS. Suit here is one of the four card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside hearts, clubs and spades.

clue.text: Failure of French action

parts.note: a feat is a notable action

explanation.surface: A failure of French military action.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss or reversal in battle or contest is a failure; the noun senses match.

clue.text: Corresponds about familiar paintings and poetry etc

indicators.note: about says one word goes round the other

parts.note: near means close or familiar, as a near relation

explanation.surface: Correspondence about well-known paintings and poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings, poetry, music and sculpture are the creative arts valued for beauty.

clue.text: Greeting central character in romance — what a fantastic literary hero

indicators.note: central character in picks the middle letter of the word that follows
fantastic says the letters of the two words are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A greeting for the main character in a romance: what a fantastic hero of literature!
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of ROMANCE is A; 'fantastic' turns WHAT A into WATHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ojibwe hero of Longfellow's narrative poem is a literary protagonist.

clue.text: American cowboys, those in dispute

definitions.meaning: in the American West, cowboys who herd horses are called this
people who argue noisily and at length

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: ranch hands tending horses, and quarrelsome arguers.

clue.text: English boozer used by man full of mystery

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

clue.text: Speak in clubs about poetry

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone recites in nightclubs, talking about poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk with someone is to speak; the verb senses match.

clue.text: Hear end of shanty that's easy to remember

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Listen to the close of a sea song that sticks in your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is instantly memorable and appealing is described this way.

clue.text: 'Hard hearted girl', girl in hot hospital

indicators.note: in places the girl's name between the two single letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the 1920s song title 'Hard Hearted Hannah', so the girl is named by her song.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the old jazz song is the girl described as hard hearted.

clue.text: VIP in recently taken photograph

explanation.surface: A celebrity appears in a recently snapped photo.

explanation.definitionFit: An important or highly successful person is informally a big shot.

clue.text: US political movement from Pennsylvania breaching new treaty

new says the letters of the word are given a fresh order

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reworks the letters into TEARTY, and 'breaching' sets the state abbreviation inside them. The Tea Party movement is named after the Boston Tea Party of 1773.
explanation.definitionFit: The conservative grassroots movement founded around 2009 takes its name from the Boston protest.

clue.text: Article about female, deathly pale

indicators.note: about says one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: A news story about a woman who looks deathly pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the grey colour of ash, as a frightened face does.

clue.text: Horrified at hag's brew

indicators.note: brew says the letters are stirred up like a witch's potion

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled by the potion a witch is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck with horror and shock is a direct synonym.

clue.text: An environmentalist almost gives consent

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, as an is

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner nearly gives approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To say yes to a proposal is to consent; both are verbs.

clue.text: Examination in ethics Ms fails to attend

indicators.note: fails to attend says the letters named are missing from the word

parts.note: the letters M and S taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ms' looks like a title for a woman; it is just the letters M and S, removed from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, such as a viva, is an oral examination.

clue.text: Couple smack child

explanation.surface: A pair of parents slap their youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is to couple, as a trailer is joined to a car.

clue.text: Oxide, thin on the ground

explanation.surface: An oxide is scarce on the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thin on the ground' looks like a single phrase for scarce; it splits into thin, link 'on', and the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths were originally isolated as oxides, so the term names such an oxide.

clue.text: Overcome with anxiety, wanted social reforms

indicators.note: reforms says the letters of the two words are made over into new order
